title: herdr evaluation spike: go/no-go and exact pin
body:
**Source:** issue #123 Phase 1

## Outcome
A timeboxed evaluation of herdr against the current Claude Code and Codex versions, ending in an explicit go/no-go and an exact herdr pin.

## Acceptance
- [ ] Timebox declared before starting; the record is written as-is when it expires
- [ ] `docs/planning/decisions/K1-herdr-evaluation.md` records go/no-go, the exact herdr version and release tag, and support per OS (Linux, macOS, Windows), every fact cited to the tagged release
- [ ] Each confirmed or refuted individually: named-session start with no attached terminal; `agent start --kind claude` and `--kind codex` accept arbitrary argv and cwd, including `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:<name>`; `agent prompt --wait`, `agent wait --until`, `agent read`, `pane wait-output`, and `agent send-keys` each take an explicit timeout; dialog text is readable through `agent read` before any keystroke; Codex's documented `unknown` state after a response
- [ ] Launch-environment delta recorded: every injected `HERDR_*` variable, and harness `settings.json`, `hooks.json`, and `config.toml` unchanged, with `integration install` never run
- [ ] Row `herdr (test tooling)` added to the `docs/planning/PINS.md` pin table with `Gates affected: none`; `**Last updated:**` bumped
- [ ] Apache-2.0 license recorded under a dev/test-tooling, not-shipped heading in `docs/planning/v0.1/07-repository-and-dependencies.md` §5
- [ ] No spike code committed; UNVERIFIED items closed with evidence or listed open

**Skills:** `oac-evidence`, `oac-gates`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Mechanical check: no herdr in product paths, no credentials in the driver
body:
**Source:** issue #123 Phase 2; ADR-001 boundaries 3, 4, 13

## Outcome
A build-failing check that herdr never reaches product code and that driver code never touches harness credentials or harness config.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `scripts/check-herdr-containment.mjs` fails on any `herdr` or `HERDR_` match in git-tracked files under `adapters/`, `core/`, `cli/`, `transports/`, or `spec/`, and on any workspace or package manifest outside `tools/herdr/` that references `tools/herdr`
- [ ] It fails on credential access or harness-config mutation in code under `tools/herdr/`: `auth.json`, `.credentials.json`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, keyring or keychain access, `integration install`
- [ ] A missing product path reports pending, not pass, as `references/mechanical-checks.md` defines it
- [ ] `--self-test` plants one violation per rule in a temporary tree and exits non-zero on each
- [ ] Added as checks 9 and 10 to `.claude/skills/oac-boundaries/references/mechanical-checks.md` with current status; the `oac-boundaries` Mechanical checks section names the script
- [ ] `.github/workflows/boundary-lint.yml` runs it on push and pull request on a GitHub-hosted runner with no secrets
- [ ] `oac-boundaries` check 3 stays clean against the script itself; `node scripts/check-skills.mjs` passes

**Skills:** `oac-boundaries`, `oac-authoring-skills`

title: herdr driver core: session lifecycle, bounded waits, capture, redaction, run manifest
body:
**Source:** issue #123 Phase 2

## Outcome
A test-only Node driver under `tools/herdr/` that wraps the herdr CLI and records every run well enough to stand beside a human-operated gate transcript.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `node tools/herdr/run.mjs --scenario <name>`; Node built-ins only, no `package.json`; herdr invoked as an external process, never linked
- [ ] Refuses to run unless `herdr --version` equals the `herdr (test tooling)` row in `docs/planning/PINS.md`
- [ ] Each run gets its own named herdr session and a scratch directory outside the repo; the session is torn down on success, failure, and timeout
- [ ] Every herdr wait carries an explicit timeout; a timeout ends the run as `NOT RUN` and never re-submits a prompt
- [ ] Per-run `run-manifest.json`: driver commit, herdr version, harness versions, OS, verbatim launch argv, `HERDR_*` env delta, harness config hashes before and after, timebox start and end, and every herdr command with its role (`operator-input`, `dialog-accept`, `wait`, `read`)
- [ ] `tools/herdr/lib/redact.mjs` strips home paths, usernames, hostnames, and tokens and reports `droppedHazardLines`, `residualLeaks`, `residualGenericHits`; on the committed G1 Box C fixture it reports zero residual hits
- [ ] Scenarios take launch commands as parameters, not hard-coded argv
- [ ] `--scenario smoke` launches a plain shell pane, reads it, and leaves no herdr process behind
- [ ] `tools/herdr/` added to the resolved layout in `docs/planning/v0.1/07-repository-and-dependencies.md` §1 as dev/test only, never a workspace member
- [ ] `node scripts/check-herdr-containment.mjs` and `oac-boundaries` checks 3 and 8 stay clean

**Skills:** `oac-implementation`, `oac-testing`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Proof of concept: G1 re-run through the driver, compared to Box C
body:
**Source:** issue #123 Phase 2

## Outcome
G1 re-run end to end through the driver on the current Claude Code version, with fixtures and a criterion-by-criterion comparison against the human-run Box C. Not verdict-bearing.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `tools/herdr/scenarios/g1-claude-wake.mjs` runs `channel-server.mjs.throwaway-quarantined` from a copy in the run directory whose sha256 matches the committed file; the file is never edited or imported
- [ ] Launch is `claude --dangerously-load-development-channels server:g1spike`, verbatim; every notification comes from the channel server's triggers, never typed by herdr
- [ ] Dialog text captured verbatim from the pane before any keystroke; the origin of the accept (driver or human) is recorded, and a driver-sent accept is not scored as meeting criterion 5
- [ ] The run covers every Box C probe: idle wake, the `<channel>` attribute query, the non-identifier-safe `meta` key, two mid-turn notifications during a busy turn, and a `reply` tool call
- [ ] Mid-turn timing is established from wire timestamps against pane text, never from herdr agent state
- [ ] Redacted `transcript-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<version>-herdr.jsonl` and `pane-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<version>-herdr.txt` under `docs/planning/gates/fixtures/g1-claude-wake/`, with `MANIFEST.json` entries; `node scripts/check-fixture-manifest.mjs` passes
- [ ] `docs/planning/gates/herdr-runs/G1-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` scores each of the five criteria against Box C as equivalent, not equivalent, or not evaluable, and includes the method-sequence diff from `tools/herdr/lib/compare-transcripts.mjs`; the run manifest sits beside it
- [ ] G1 verdict and the `STATUS.md` G1 row unchanged; `G1-result.md` gains only a pointer to the herdr run
- [ ] If the observed Claude Code version differs from the PINS.md last-observed version, the run stops and reports a pin-move trigger; no PINS.md edit here

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-claude-channels`, `oac-testing`, `oac-boundaries`

title: Fold scripted runs into the gate and test methodology
body:
**Source:** issue #123 Phase 3

## Outcome
The gate and test methodology states how a herdr-driven run is recorded, what it may conclude, and when it may carry a verdict.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `.claude/skills/oac-gates/references/scripted-runs.md` added and linked from `oac-gates`: driver identity, timebox for scripted runs, timeout means `NOT RUN`, no automatic re-submission
- [ ] Rule stated: herdr agent state is a scheduling signal only; criteria are scored on OAC's wire transcript plus verbatim pane text
- [ ] Verdict eligibility stated: a scripted run of G<n> is non-verdict-bearing until an equivalence record for G<n> exists at the current herdr pin, and reverts on any herdr pin move
- [ ] Driver-sent accepts of operator-consent dialogs (G1 criterion 5, the G11 confirmation) carry an explicit rule taken from a recorded operator decision, not assumed
- [ ] `docs/planning/gates/README.md`: extended template gains `Driver:`; the `-herdr` fixture suffix and `docs/planning/gates/herdr-runs/` documented; a herdr pin move invalidates equivalence records, never gate verdicts
- [ ] `.claude/skills/oac-testing/SKILL.md` §1-§2 and `docs/planning/v0.1/09-test-strategy.md`: herdr-driven runs are provider-integration tier, opt-in by construction, never default
- [ ] `scripts/check-fixture-manifest.mjs` requires a `driver` block (`herdr_version`, `driver_commit`, `run_manifest`) on every `-herdr` fixture entry; K4's entries pass
- [ ] `node scripts/check-skills.mjs` passes

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-testing`, `oac-authoring-skills`, `oac-evidence`

title: Opt-in CI job on operator-owned runners
body:
**Source:** issue #123 Phase 4

## Outcome
An opt-in workflow that runs a driver scenario on operator-owned, already-logged-in runners and publishes only redacted evidence.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `.github/workflows/herdr-provider-optin.yml` triggers only on `workflow_dispatch` (input `scenario`) and on `push` to `main` touching `docs/planning/PINS.md`; no `pull_request` or `pull_request_target` trigger
- [ ] Jobs run on `[self-hosted, oac-harness, linux]` and `[self-hosted, oac-harness, windows]`, one concurrent run per runner
- [ ] No provider secret or API key referenced; nothing reads, copies, or uploads harness credentials, and harness login stays the runner operator's
- [ ] Artifacts are the redacted transcript, pane capture, and run manifest only, uploaded only after a clean residual scan; the scratch directory is deleted afterward
- [ ] `docs/planning/gates/herdr-runner.md` states runner prerequisites: pinned herdr, interactive harness login by the operator, runner labels, and that fork PRs never reach these runners
- [ ] One successful G1 dispatch on Linux and one on Windows, run URLs recorded in `herdr-runner.md`
- [ ] No other workflow references herdr; the default tier is unchanged

**Skills:** `oac-testing`, `oac-security-work`, `oac-boundaries`

title: G2 driver scenario: Codex live inject with bounded `unknown`-state handling
body:
**Source:** issue #123 Phase 5

## Outcome
G2 re-run through the driver on the current Codex version, with fixtures and a comparison against the human-run `0.157.1` re-run. Not verdict-bearing.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `tools/herdr/scenarios/g2-codex-inject.mjs` runs `codex app-server daemon start`, then plain `codex` with no config overrides via `agent start --kind codex`, and records the pane's process argv as proof
- [ ] Delivery into the live thread goes only through a second app-server client (`thread/queue/add` or `turn/start`), never typed by herdr; `client.mjs.throwaway-quarantined` runs from a sha256-matched copy if it works unmodified on the current version, otherwise the divergence is recorded
- [ ] Turn completion comes from the app-server event stream or `pane wait-output` with a timeout; an `unknown` state never triggers a re-submit
- [ ] The driver never reads `CODEX_HOME/auth.json` or the keyring
- [ ] Redacted `-herdr` transcript and pane fixtures under `docs/planning/gates/fixtures/g2-codex-inject/`, with `MANIFEST.json` entries carrying the `schema` and `driver` blocks
- [ ] `docs/planning/gates/herdr-runs/G2-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` scores all four G2 criteria against the human-run fixture
- [ ] G2 verdict and `STATUS.md` unchanged; a version mismatch against PINS.md is reported as a pin-move trigger, not edited here

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-codex-appserver`, `oac-testing`, `oac-boundaries`

title: G4 and G5 driver scenarios, and the reuse contract for Stage 4 and 5 tests
body:
**Source:** issue #123 Phase 5

## Outcome
Driver scenarios for G4 and G5, plus the documented contract Stage 4 provider-integration and Stage 5 end-to-end tests reuse. Not verdict-bearing.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `tools/herdr/scenarios/g4-mcp-dual-era.mjs` and `g5-provenance.mjs`, with servers under `tools/herdr/gate-servers/` rebuilt from the architecture in `G4-result.md` and `G5-result.md` because the original spike servers were never committed; each comparison doc says so
- [ ] G4 runs the legacy and `2026-07-28` paths concurrently, and the `2026-07-28` channel-rejection negative case explicitly
- [ ] Codex MCP registration uses per-invocation or project-scoped configuration; the operator's global Codex config is never edited and `CODEX_HOME` is never copied
- [ ] G5 spoofing bodies reach the harness only through the channel server or the app-server client, never typed by herdr
- [ ] Redacted `-herdr` fixtures and `MANIFEST.json` entries for both gates; `docs/planning/gates/herdr-runs/G4-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` and `G5-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md` score every criterion against the recorded result; G4 and G5 verdicts unchanged
- [ ] `tools/herdr/README.md` documents reuse by G4/G7 provider-integration tests and H1/H4: G11's OAC-enabled launch commands passed as scenario parameters, tests placed under top-level `tests/integration/`, runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows
- [ ] `node scripts/check-herdr-containment.mjs` stays clean

**Skills:** `oac-gates`, `oac-testing`, `oac-claude-channels`, `oac-codex-appserver`, `oac-mcp`
